facts.value: Once ASU has received all documents required to issue an I-20 and has verified that they are complete, you will receive an email with a link to download your I-20 from the Document Portal in My ASU. Once received, you should print the I-20 and sign the document.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: You will not receive a physical I-20 via mail.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: The email will be sent to your non-ASU personal email address. Be sure to check it often, including junk and spam folders, so you do not miss any messages.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: Once you have received your I-20, be sure to pay your I-901 fee. Once the fee has been paid do not delay in contacting your consulate to obtain a visa appointment.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: Some consulates may have long wait times, so do not delay on securing an appointment time.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: If you are unable to submit the documentation needed to receive an I-20 from ASU or are unable to obtain your F1 visa in time to arrive by the start of the semester of your admission, contact [email protected] and we can advise you on your options.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: If you have any questions, please contact our International Admission Services team. We will work with you to keep you on track.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: View the I-20 Frequently Asked Questions webpage for more information.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: Be sure to check wait times for your local embassy or consulate, as some areas may be experiencing wait times longer than 30 days.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: You can now apply for your visa up to 365 days before the start date listed on your I-20.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: Complete these steps as soon as possible so that when your local embassy can take your appointment, you will be ready to proceed with your next steps.

metadata.chunk_title: What we want you to know + Helpful reminder

facts.value: If you are residing in the U.S. on a valid visa, you will need to provide proof of your current visa.
If you are a current high school student, you can earn university credit.

metadata.chunk_title: Programme Overview + If you are a current high school student, you can earn university credit.

facts.value: There are no employer or location restrictions for authorized STEM OPT, but the job must be in the U.S.
You must carry your I-20, passport, and valid F-1 visa stamp to re-enter the U.S.
Entering the U.S. on any visa other than F-1 will invalidate your F-1 status and STEM OPT.
The primary purpose of Post-OPT/STEM is working; taking classes can be incidental.
Pursuing a new degree program will invalidate your Post-OPT/STEM once you receive the new degree I-20.
There is a 60-day grace period after Post-OPT/STEM ends to change visa status, transfer, or return home.
Changing your address while your STEM OPT application is pending may cause issues with your EAD card.
You must update your address through MyUSCIS, USPS, and MyASU within 10 days of moving.
Your SEVP Portal account will lock after 3 consecutive incorrect password entries or 45 days of inactivity.
To reset your password, follow the steps to reset using your ASU Public Email and SEVIS ID.
You can check the status of your application by logging into your USCIS online application.
The ISSC takes up to 7 days to process Post-OPT/STEM requests; USCIS average processing time is 90 days.
